abstract:
Incomplete molecular assays and small labelled cancer cohorts limit survival prediction and transfer.
We present UniPanSurv, a model that shares a backbone across cancers and scores directed relations among retained, observed molecules. It pools these relations into separate summaries while leaving molecular tokens unchanged. A discrete-time head predicts survival curves. The model uses an Unknown context for zero-shot prediction and lightweight updates for few-shot adaptation. The common-input cancer-macro C-index was 0.752. In matched 10- and 20-shot comparisons with MMOSurv, C-index differences were 0.019 (95% CI, 0.0091 to 0.0296) and 0.018 (95% CI, 0.0088 to 0.0278), respectively. Patient-level bootstrap intervals are conditional on the fitted models. The confidence interval for the C-index difference from the closest common-input comparator includes zero. Database support does not establish causal molecular interactions.
